newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares close lower, depressed by Astra.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares close lower, depressed by Astra.

text.p: Sweden's sharemarket closed lower on Tuesday, slipping for the second consecutive day from last Friday's record high close, with drugs major Astra depressing the market.
The lower U.S. open on Wall Street during afternoon trade did nothing to boost the tone.
The Stockholm general index closed 0.58 percent lower at 2,043.38 after shares worth 3.2 billion crowns changed hands.
Astra was a major market focus, leading the drugs sector down 1.44 percent as it slipped five crowns to close at 281 crowns.
"It seems like there are many traders who are in Astra for the short term and are now selling," one analyst said.

A decision to allow parallel imports into Sweden of Astra's ulcer treatment Losec from other parts of Europe could have something to do with the fall, the analyst said. Astra said the decision could lead to lower prices on the drug.
Construction company NCC rose 1.50 crowns to 77 on Monday's news that that it would buy the Danish contracting operations of Denmark's Rasmussen & Schiotz.
Engineering firm Atlas Copco rose 2.50 crowns to 139 in lively trade.
The forestry sector index slid 1.23 percent, possibly due to the strengthening of the crown, one analyst said.
